newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hugo Boss plans to launch women's collection in 98. [CORRECTED 14:37 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hugo Boss plans to launch women's collection in 98. [CORRECTED 14:37 GMT]

text.p: German men's fashion retailer Hugo Boss said on Monday it planned to broaden its position in the fashion world, preparing to launch a women's collection early next year.

In a mandatory German bourse statement the group, which is majority held by Italy's Marzotto Group, also said it would begin marketing a women's scent, Hugo Woman, as a counterpart to its Hugo fragrance, this August.
"In January 1998 we plan to launch a collection for the fashion conscious woman aged between 20 and 40 years old," the group said in the statement.
The group plans to hold a news conference in Stuttgart today.
As reported earlier this year, Boss also said it would pay out almost all of its 1996 profits to shareholders through a special dividend and an increase in the regular dividends.

Boss tied the higher dividend payout to an almost 30 percent increase in 1996 group net profit to 76.1 (corrects from 75.2) million marks ($45.1 million) and a 10.5 percent increase in sales to 995.3 million marks.
The company said it raised the payout per ordinary share to 45 marks from 41 marks in 1995 and to 46.50 marks from 42.50 marks for each preference share.
In addition Boss said it would make a special payment of 57 marks per share. The dividend payouts will total 65.8 million marks compared with 26.7 million marks in 1995, Boss said.
The group's earnings per share, as calculated on the DVFA method, jumped by 107 marks from 97 marks in 1995.

Boss has seen strong growth from its decision to split its product lines into three groups from one -- Boss for traditional buyers, Hugo for younger, more contemporary buyers and Baldessarini for top-line customers.

But the company has been hampered by leadership issues after Boss Chief Executive Peter Littmann, 49, left the firm at the start of 1997 after an apparent dispute with Marzotto officials over the direction of the Stuttgart- based group.
Joachim Vogt, a 44-year-old production and logistics executive at Boss, has taken over as management board chairman from Littmann.

Despite the leadership questions, Boss said in January that it expected sales for the first half of 1997 to rise about five percent to 475 million marks, buoyed by strong sales for the Hugo brand and the Baldessarini brand.
Boss executives have said they were particularly looking for stronger sales in Spain, Britain, eastern Europe, Asia and South America. ($ = 1.685 German Marks)
